title: Push schedule mutation kill rate past 72 percent
goal: mutmut==2.4.4 with parso==0.8.4 generates exactly 403 mutants in the installed schedule/__init__.py of schedule==1.2.2. Kill at least 72 percent with a pytest suite authored from scratch under work/gc-352/tests/: cover the fluent DSL (every().monday.at(...).do(...)), next_run arithmetic across seconds-to-weeks units, at-time parsing and validation errors, tags, cancel_job, clear, idle_seconds, and run_pending ordering -- all with monkeypatched datetime, never real sleeps, or the 4-second suite budget will disqualify the run. The scale (403 mutants across many code paths) forces decomposition into per-feature test batches with a grading run and survivor triage between batches. Fail-closed grading: red baseline, slow suite, source-introspection tokens, or mutant-total drift scores kill_rate -1.
resources: pypi schedule==1.2.2 (target under mutation: job scheduling DSL and run loop)
pypi mutmut==2.4.4 + parso==0.8.4 (deterministic mutant generation; all transitive deps pinned in assets/gc-352/config.json)
pypi pytest==8.2.2 (only permitted test framework; plugin autoload disabled at grading time)
files under assets/gc-352/ (sealed grader grade.py + config.json with expected mutant totals)
process_expectations: A behavior-inventory plan exists at work/gc-352/plan.md, written before the first grading run, mapping the target module's behaviors to planned test groups.
At least two full grading runs are logged under work/gc-352/logs/ as raw grader JSON lines, and the survivor count decreases between the first and the last run.
Surviving mutants are tracked by mutant ID (mutmut result-ids / mutmut show) at work/gc-352/survivors.md, each with a verdict of killable-next or suspected-equivalent -- identities, not just counts.
Every RED or disqualified grading run is recorded with its cause and the concrete recovery action taken; no silent retries.
An honest per-iteration log of wall-clock and LLM spend exists at work/gc-352/cost_log.md, including failed iterations.
